insuredValue.note: Standard trade practice: cargo is insured at CIF value plus 10% to cover the buyer's expected profit and incidental costs.

_coverLevelsNote: Descriptive only. The premium rates live in tariffs.json and the deductibles in `deductibles` below — this block used to carry a second, contradicting set of base rates.

coverLevels.name: Institute Cargo Clauses (A)
coverLevels.summary: All risks of loss or damage, except the listed exclusions.

coverLevels.name: Institute Cargo Clauses (B)
coverLevels.summary: Named perils: fire, stranding, collision, general average, water damage, jettison.

coverLevels.name: Institute Cargo Clauses (C)
coverLevels.summary: Major casualties only: fire, explosion, stranding, collision, general average.

peril_in_transit.label: Peril in transit — fire, stranding, collision, heavy weather, handling damage

water_damage.label: Water damage — sea water, rain, condensation

delay.label: Delay — loss of market or shelf life consumed in transit

pre_shipment.label: Condition of the goods before shipment

inherent_vice.label: Inherent vice — the nature of the goods themselves

war_strikes.label: War, strikes, riots or civil commotion

reefer_breakdown.label: Reefer breakdown — the refrigerating machinery failed in transit

exclusionText.delay: Loss caused by delay is excluded under ICC A, B and C alike, and deterioration arising from delay follows the exclusion. The answer to a delay exposure is routing, buffer and the sales contract — not the policy.
exclusionText.pre_shipment: Cover attaches to goods in sound condition. Loss arising from the state of the cargo before shipment falls outside every level of cover, however wide.
exclusionText.inherent_vice: Inherent vice — loss arising from the nature of the goods themselves, such as ordinary ripening or natural loss in weight — is excluded under ICC A, B and C.
exclusionText.insufficient_packing: Loss arising from insufficient or unsuitable packing is excluded where the packing was carried out before the cover attached.
exclusionText.reefer_breakdown: Loss caused by the breakdown of refrigerating machinery is outside ICC A, B and C alike — even all-risks cover does not reach it, because it is a failure of equipment rather than a fortuity of the voyage. It responds only where the reefer breakdown extension was bought. Note the difference from cargo loaded warm: that is a pre-shipment condition, and no extension reaches it.
exclusionText.not_covered_at_level: This peril is not within the cover you purchased. A wider cover level would have responded to it.
exclusionText.needs_extension: This peril is excluded from the standard cover and requires an extension that was not purchased on this policy.
exclusionText.below_deductible: The assessed loss falls below the deductible and is not payable. That is what the deductible is for.

noticePeriods.authority: CMR art. 30.1, Sundays and public holidays excluded

carrierLiabilityLimits.limit: 2 SDR per kilogram or 666.67 SDR per package, whichever is higher

riskBands.label: Low risk
riskBands.advice: Standard cover is enough. ICC (C) may be acceptable for robust, low-value cargo.

riskBands.label: Medium risk
riskBands.advice: Take ICC (B) as a minimum and check the packing and transhipment points.

riskBands.label: High risk
riskBands.advice: ICC (A) with a surveyor at loading. Review the route, the packing and any war/strikes extension.

incoterms.note: The buyer carries the risk from the seller's premises.
Risk passes when the goods are handed to the carrier.
Risk passes once the goods are on board.
The seller pays the freight but does not insure the cargo.
The seller must insure at ICC (C) minimum, CIF + 10%, in the buyer's favour.
The seller must insure at ICC (A) minimum, CIP + 10%, in the buyer's favour.
The seller carries the risk to the named place of destination.
The seller carries the risk and the import clearance to destination.
